description: The scorer's headline flag (survives_both_windows AND rw_survives_both_windows) carries no evidence of skill at this n. A sign-flip null over the 74 margin h=0 PIT cells (one sign vector per draw applied to every cell, so cross-cell correlation is preserved) yields 22.1 survivors on average (median 16, 5-95 pct [1,61], max 72); the run observed 25. P(null >= observed) = 0.39; per-cell null survival probability 0.298 vs an observed rate of 0.338. Excluding M5, which starts from the consensus: 11 observed against a null mean of 16.9, P = 0.54. W2's 10 quarters are a SUBSET of W1's 14 and the two weightings are highly correlated, so the flag is close to free. 30 of the 201 scored margin cells carry it.
proposed_fix: Stop presenting the survivor list as a ranking. Put a paired-loss p-value and a quarters-better count next to every MAE ratio; or state plainly that no margin object in this run is distinguishable from seasonal naive at h=0.

description: Of the 59 surviving margin cell-windows, 9 reach p<0.05 on a paired loss differential against seasonal naive (d_q = |e_method| - |e_naive|, Newey-West(1) SE) and EVERY ONE IS W2-ONLY - not a single cell is significant in W1. Seven of the nine are M5 street-bias cells, which begin from the Street consensus and inherit its lift over y[q-4]; the other two are M3's pin specs (rw_hl4_pin p 0.033, last_pin p 0.006), which are better in only 3 of 10 and 7 of 10 quarters. For every method built from the company's own history (M1, M2, M4, M6, M7) the largest W1 |t| is 0.83 and every W1 p exceeds 0.40.
proposed_fix: Quote every MAE ratio with its paired-test p-value, its n and the quarters-better count. Drop 'beats the naive' language where p>0.2.

description: Seven registered specs feed the ACTUAL revenue (or nights) into rows labelled prior_basis=PIT, in the same registry and scoreboard as genuine PIT specs, distinguished only by a substring of spec_id: driver-lines e_revknown_rw (margin_v2, lines_v2), cycle-flex revknown_rw (flex_margin, flex_lines), margin-ts k4_rw_revknown / drift_k4_rw_revknown / g_k4_rw_nightsknown, guide-policy-margin rw_hl4_revknown. M_common rule 6 permits a revenue-known diagnostic, but FORMAT 1.0 does not mark it, and the best margin cell in the whole run by MAE (1.96pp, W1 h=0) is one of them.
proposed_fix: Add an explicit boolean column (revenue_known) to the registry frames, or agree a spec-id prefix the scorer excludes. Until then WS20/23 must filter on the substrings revknown / nightsknown.

description: Spec d_steps_rw reads WS04 step dummies straight out of M1's module-level PANEL (design_rows and forecast_quarter) and never consults 04_signal_knowable_from.csv. event_E09_cor_cash is dated ON from 2025Q1 but became knowable only 2026-02-12; event_E10_pd_cash is ON from 2023Q1, knowable 2023-03-01. 7 of the 14 W1 guide dates and 6 of the 10 W2 dates fit or forecast with a step regressor that was not public. M4 gates the identical signals correctly via known(ks[q], vd).
proposed_fix: Gate the step level by knowable_from at every vintage and re-run. Until then d_steps_rw is not a PIT spec and its rows must not be quoted.

description: M3 is the only method whose note has no commit predating its results: pre-registration and results landed together in 5bd8fb5 (M1/M2/M7 pre-registered at d5da4e4, M6 at bebbf4e, M4 at fdf3447). The amendment states that the pre-registration lists five cushion specs plus rw_hl4_pin and rw_hl4_revknown, but the pre-registration paragraph as written lists only rw_hl4, equal, last, nocushion and rw_hl4_prorata. On the note's own text both passing specs (rw_hl4_pin, last_pin) are post-hoc, while the pre-registered main spec rw_hl4 fails (3.83pp W1 / 1.97pp W2).
proposed_fix: M3 to state which specs existed on disk before the first fit. Until then the pin result is exploratory: a hypothesis for 5 Nov, not a backtested pass.

description: The pin's MAE win is tail-driven, not accuracy. rw_hl4_pin beats seasonal naive in 4 of 14 W1 quarters and 3 of 10 W2 quarters. The entire W1 gain is 2023Q4 (single-quarter gain -3.18pp); excluding that quarter the pin is WORSE than seasonal naive by +0.19pp. last_pin: 8/14 W1, again all of the gain in 2023Q4, +0.22pp without it. In W2 a gain survives the exclusion (-0.32pp) but the quarter count does not.
proposed_fix: Describe the pin as clipping the break quarters (2023Q4 carries the $931M lodging-tax reserve year end), not as quarter-to-quarter accuracy.

description: q_sentence_direction was generated by WS10's full-sample observation that the quarterly-sentence direction rule is 13/14 right, then tested on those same 14 quarters. The direction is non-zero in 13 of 14 W1 quarters, of which 9 are -1 and 4 are +1, with only 3 sign changes along the W1 sequence (2 in W2). A constant always-negative rule agrees with the sign of the realised y/y change 8 of 13 times, so the incremental content rests on 4 positive-direction quarters, 3 of them in the 2023 recovery.
proposed_fix: Present the sentence rule as a descriptive regularity with an effective n of 4 direction changes, not as a tested forecaster. Its MAE ratio (0.92 W1) has t = -0.22.

description: beats_seasonal_naive and the survives_both_windows flags are asserted on as few as 2 matched quarters (score.py requires m.sum() >= 2). guide-policy-margin/q4_implied|guide_mid carries survives_both_windows = yes on n=3, with MAE 2.87pp and a -2.87pp bias.
proposed_fix: Suppress the flags below n=8, or carry n beside every flag in the scoreboard markdown so WS20 cannot quote an n=3 pass.

description: The baselines write prior_basis INTO spec_id (e.g. street|adj_ebitda_margin_pct|h0|PIT) and the margin scorer keys on spec_id, so replays_present = 1 for all 1,452 baseline scoreboard rows while the seven methods correctly report 2. The two-replay rule reads as violated for every baseline object.
proposed_fix: Drop prior_basis from the baseline spec_id, or exclude spec_id from the replays_present group key in score.py.

description: The intervals are systematically too WIDE, not too narrow. Mean cov80 on adj_ebitda_margin_pct at h=0 PIT is 0.930 over 63 cells against a nominal 0.80; 21 of 126 margin cells sit above the n=14 binomial 5-95 band and none sit below it. Below EBITDA: op_margin 1.00, pretax 1.00, op_income 0.99, interest income 0.98, sbc_pct_rev 0.99, eps 0.97. M7's self-reported tax under-coverage (tax_provision 0.762, tax_rate 0.796) lies INSIDE the n=14 band and is not supportable; the only genuinely low cell is capex at 0.643, at the band edge.
proposed_fix: Re-derive the 5 Nov band from the realised h=0 error distribution rather than the Gaussian-on-last-12 pool, which over-disperses. Withdraw the tax under-coverage claim as an n=14 statement.

description: The three driver/flex models put 3Q26 at 51.2-51.6% (M1 and M4 51.57, M6 51.23) against a 3Q25 actual of 50.09% and the CEILING sentence in force from the 2Q26 letter of 6 Aug 2026 (margin roughly flat to slightly down y/y). Their LIVE h=0 forecast contradicts the guidance the same run uses as a baseline elsewhere and sits 1.4-1.8pp above Street (49.78%). M1's own note attributes the gap to the S&M line.
proposed_fix: Either argue the exception explicitly (why management's ceiling is wrong) or clip to the sentence as M3 does. A 3Q26 above 50.09% cannot go on the card unargued.

description: M3's registered LIVE path (rw_hl4_pin, base revenue) puts 4Q26 at 34.51% and 4Q27 at 34.30%, both above every historical Q4 in 2022-26 (range 26.6-33.3%) and 5.6pp above Street's 4Q26 of 28.90%; the implied FY26 is 37.03%, 1.53pp above the 35.5% floor in force. The mechanism is the FY budget identity after the Q3 pin: the residual lands in Q4. M3's own note prefers 30.9% under the modal November sentence.
proposed_fix: Carry M3's sentence scenario (4Q26 30.9%), not the registered rw_hl4_pin LIVE row, into the combined model; or register the sentence scenario as its own spec.

description: Three packages' run.py read gitignored inputs with no re-pull fallback: M6 two LSEG peer files under data/raw/margin_build/04_alt_signals/misc (manifested under WS04, not under M6), M7 three FRED daily files under data/raw/margin_build/M7_below_ebitda (manifested; its README says re-pull by hand), WS03 the Bloomberg local file. From a clean checkout each raises FileNotFoundError before writing anything, so the brief's rule that run.py rebuilds the package end to end with exit 0 holds only on this machine.
proposed_fix: Add a fetch-if-missing branch for the keyless FRED pulls (WS04 already has one); document licensed prerequisites at the top of each README and in M6's own manifest.

description: 31 of 58 (method, spec, window) cells at h=0 show the five cash LINES beating seasonal naive on average (mean MAE ratio 0.51-0.78) while the MARGIN loses to it (ratio > 1) - including M1's own main spec b_elastic_rw in W1 (lines 0.53, margin 1.010) and M4's best1 specs (lines 0.51-0.59, margin 1.09-1.10). Seasonal naive is a weak baseline for a growing dollar series and a strong one for a ratio, so a line-level MAE ratio is close to free. This confirms and generalises M4's cross-method warning.
proposed_fix: Re-score every line claim on adj_ebitda_margin_pct before quoting it, and name the line baseline used (seasonal_naive_drift or pct_rev_last4, not seasonal_naive).

description: M6's FY28 forecast (31.3% vs Street 37.7%) compounds positive fitted growth intercepts over four unanchored quarters. M6 flags it itself; repeated here so the flag survives synthesis.
proposed_fix: Drop M6's FY28 row or replace it with a flat-margin roll-forward, labelled.

description: M7's backtested EPS and FCF chains take their EBITDA input from a harness BASELINE (q_guide_implied, else guide_implied, else seasonal_naive_drift), so the ebitda_pit object's error is dominated by that baseline rather than by the below-the-line model. Only the ebitda_known variant measures M7's own accuracy, and prior_basis does not separate the two.
proposed_fix: Quote M7's below-the-line accuracy from ebitda_known and total EPS error from ebitda_pit, never mixing them.

description: history_as_of includes the same-day letter (include_same_day=True), so every h=0 forecast in this run uses the letter and the guidance sentence published that evening. This is the frozen revenue-harness convention, applied consistently, but it means h=0 is a post-letter, post-guide forecast rather than a pre-print one.
proposed_fix: Say so on the card: the models forecast the quarter AFTER the guide is given, which is not the position a trade into the 5 Nov print occupies for 4Q26.

description: M2's LIVE comparison columns are LSEG values from 06_consensus_quarterly_2027.csv pulled 2026-09-13, on rows stamped vintage_date 2026-09-11. Comparison columns only, not inputs, so no leakage and no kill-list breach, but the stamp is wrong.
proposed_fix: Stamp the comparison column with its own pull date, separate from vintage_date.

description: Every pre-registration in this run is self-attested inside its own note. M1, M2 and M7 have a genuine pre-results commit (d5da4e4), M6 at bebbf4e and M4 at fdf3447; M3 does not (R05). Nothing else can be checked against a timestamp.
proposed_fix: For stages 20-32, commit the pass line before the fit runs.

description: Clean replay under py -3.13 from the worktree root: every package's run.py exits 0 (see 21_reproducibility.csv for exit codes and wall times). The only files that differ after the replay are build-stamp JSONs containing a timestamp; every registry file and every processed CSV regenerated byte-identical.
proposed_fix: none

description: No kill-list number from AGENT_BRIEF section 6 is quoted in any note, script or processed file; no close-to-known language outside the brief and the prompt quoting the rule; no consensus value used as an input outside M5 (the harness street baseline and WS03 rows are comparison columns, and street_as_of <= vintage_date on all 700 street rows); no licensed raw rows in a tracked path - data/raw is gitignored (.gitignore:28), no margin_build raw file is tracked, and the committed consensus files are derived and vendor/timestamp stamped (03_consensus_at_dates 252 rows, 03_peer_consensus_monthly 616 rows).
proposed_fix: none

description: Mechanical PIT rules pass on all 32 registry files and 87,628 rows (M5 included): zero rows with knowable_from > vintage_date, zero with street_as_of > vintage_date, zero forecasting a quarter that had already printed at the vintage, zero horizon mismatches, zero window/vintage-date inconsistencies, zero non-monotone quantile ladders, zero duplicate keys.
proposed_fix: none

description: M5's headline MARGIN claim does not survive a paired test against the raw Street baseline, while its DOLLAR claim does. dispersion_conditioned|rw_hl4 on adj_ebitda_margin_pct: W1 ratio 0.835, mean d -0.26pt, NW(1) t -0.57, p 0.57, better in 9 of 14 quarters; W2 ratio 0.567, mean d -0.57pt, t -1.46, p 0.145, better in 7 of 10. By contrast street_plus_flowthrough|rw_hl4 on adj_ebitda_musd: W2 ratio 0.581, t -2.71, p 0.007, better in 9 of 10 (sign test p 0.011); W1 ratio 0.660, t -1.39, p 0.165, better in 11 of 14 (sign test p 0.029). 4 of 144 street-bias cells beat Street at p<0.05 and all four are the same object and target in W2 across correlated specs, so it is one finding, not four - but it is the ONLY cell in the whole audit that survives an adversarial test.
proposed_fix: Quote M5's dollar-EBITDA flow-through as the run's one forecasting edge, with its p-value and quarters-better count. Do not quote the margin-point improvement (1.59 -> 1.33 / 1.31 -> 0.74) as a beat; it is inside the noise at n 14/10.

description: The dispersion regression that motivates dispersion_conditioned - the best margin object - is significant only on the sample M5's own pre-registration excludes. M5_secondary_tests.json: dispersion_signed slope +28.3 pt per unit sd/mean, se 8.8, p 0.005, R2 0.379, n 19; but dispersion_signed_from22 (the pre-registered 2022Q1+ estimation pool, which M5 argues is the only comparable regime because 2021 carried a -50.7% margin estimate) gives slope +17.1, se 8.1, p 0.052, R2 0.230, n 17. The method drops 2021 from every bias pool and then justifies its conditioning variable on a regression that keeps it.
proposed_fix: Re-state the dispersion slope on the 2022Q1+ pool (p 0.052) as the supporting number, or justify keeping 2021 for this one test.

description: dispersion_conditioned is not conditioning on dispersion in the recent regime - the clip constant is. The multiplier clip(disp/disp_ref, 0.5, 2.0) sits exactly at the 0.5 floor in 21 of 39 backtest vintage rows, and at the floor at every h=0 vintage from 2023-05 onward except three February dispersion spikes (Feb-24 1.34, Feb-25 1.93, Feb-26 0.58). In that regime the object is street_plus_bias with the bias halved by a fixed constant. At the LIVE vintage the raw ratio is 0.083 - six times below the floor, and the raw dispersion 0.0085 is below the entire backtest range (0.0198-0.2257) - so the LIVE call is a pure clip. M5 states this itself: uncapped, the 3Q26 margin call would be 49.9%, essentially the Street. The headline LIVE 3Q26 +0.41pt / +$51M beat is therefore produced by the clip bound, not by the fitted relationship.
proposed_fix: On the card, give the direction (Street low, dispersion at a record low so the beat is small) and take the point from the dollar flow-through object, not from the clipped dispersion object. If dispersion_conditioned is kept, report how often the clip binds.

description: M5's consensus inputs are point-in-time as required of the one method allowed to use consensus. Every one of the 3,888 street-bias registry rows carries street_as_of <= vintage_date (zero violations; minimum lag 0 days, which is the admissible as_of == vintage TODAY row). The 2026-08-06 LIVE vintage is genuinely PRE-guide: LSEG role guided_q_pre_guide, street_as_of 2026-08-05 (D-1), obs_date 2026-08-02, n_est 34, 3Q26 EBITDA $2,323.8M - distinct from the post-guide 11 Sep value of $2,361.5M used at the TODAY vintage. The surprise pool filters print_date <= vintage, the dispersion reference pool filters vintage_date <= vintage, and the unbacktested 1Q27-4Q27 _fyalloc rows are labelled by the author.
proposed_fix: none

description: M5's quantiles are unusable and the author says so: cov80 = cov90 = 1.00 in every scored cell, and the CRPS of the dollar objects ($73-103M) is worse than the raw Street's ($48-50M), because the PIT residual pool still contains the 2022-23 errors. This is the same over-dispersion as R10, in its most extreme form.
proposed_fix: Take the 5 Nov band from the last-8-quarter realised error distribution, not from M5's registered quantiles.
